_note: YouTube's 24 Aug 2026 view-counting change. From that date a view counts the moment a video begins to play, with no minimum watch time, across VOD/Shorts/Live. Long-form previously needed roughly 30 seconds of watch time; Shorts already counted this way (since 31 Mar 2025), which is why Shorts serve as the control group when measuring the step. Every view figure on this site that spans 24 Aug 2026 is therefore a blend of two different metrics.
_method: Measured, not assumed. scripts/measure-viewcount-change.js compares the daily view accrual of the DORMANT, NEVER-ADVERTISED back catalogue (flat decay: nothing about an old video changes on that date except how its views are counted) for 14 days either side of the change. Shorts run the same comparison as a control and should show no step. Their ratio cancels any channel-wide drift.
_method2: Second, independent estimate on NEW UPLOADS: scripts/measure-debut-curve.js, using the hourly debut samples. It reports a LEVEL (median views at 18h, before vs after) and a SHAPE (what share of day-one views has landed by 2h). The shape signal is the stronger of the two because it is a ratio within each video, so news-cycle size and video quality cancel out; the level signal is badly confounded by exactly those things and is a cross-check only. The two methods measure different traffic surfaces — back catalogue lives on search/suggested, new uploads on subscriptions/home — so if they disagree, the gap is itself the finding rather than a failure.
_precision: Measured on the existing spread, the 95% interval on the factor is roughly +/-16% at 7 days either side, +/-11% at 14 days, +/-8% at 28 days. Use whole weeks only: the daily series has a weekday cycle, and an uneven slice of it injects bias that looks exactly like a real step. Past about three weeks the limit stops being sample size and becomes whether the two windows are comparable at all, which is what the Shorts control is for. Expect to be able to say 'about a quarter, somewhere between 15% and 35%' - not a precise divisor for the revenue estimate.

expected.note: Prior from the Shorts precedent of 31 Mar 2025, when creators saw public view counts rise 20-30% on identical content.

monetisation.note: YouTube states earnings and YPP eligibility are unaffected, because payouts continue to use 'engaged views' (the old watch-time bar). Revenue estimates on this site multiply views by an RPM, so once views inflate the estimate overstates unless it is divided back down by the measured factor.

noiseFloor.note: Measured 2026-08-17 on the control group, so we know what size of step is real. Day-to-day swing in the dormant, never-advertised catalogue.
